text: Taeo read the seizure notice eleven times. Every time, the time left was shorter.
Nib didn't know the word seized. Taeo explained it meant taken away. By who? People with forms, probably. Taeo had never owned anything worth seizing.
At eight fifty-five the shouting brick went off again. Taeo jolted awake. Nib informed him it had been light for two hours.
The ability assessment office opened at nine, so they sat and stared at the phone until it did.
At nine on the dot, Taeo called. The receptionist already knew about his summoning. Eleven o'clock today. Bring your ID. And bring him.
Before they left, Taeo asked if Nib wanted shoes. No. Taeo laid down the rules. Stay close. Keep the knife in its sheath. Let me do the talking.
Nib corrected him. You don't decide where I go.
Then Nib stepped out into Seoul for the first time.
Taeo had never noticed how loud the buses were until he saw Nib flinch at them.
On World Cup-ro, summons were common, and nobody looked twice at the construct across the road. But everybody looked at Nib. Taeo's advice was simple. Look back.
Nib asked if the giant woman on the building was in charge here. She was in an advert, Taeo said. For spears? For an airline.
A screen at the bus stop showed the weekly fan ranking of hunters. Nib couldn't believe they counted who people liked.
At the assessment office, Nib fought the revolving door, and insisted he had only been checking both sides.
In the lobby, he kept the queue ticket even though they didn't need one.
On the lobby TV was Han Seoryun, an S-rank hunter, coming out of a gate. The next team is already there, she said. Mine are going home to sleep.
Taeo had watched her for years. Nib asked why. Because she kept going back for people. Her team's patch was sewn onto Taeo's backpack.
Then an assessor called his name. Yoon Taeo.
Her name was Chae. Her notes said his summon could talk. Nib confirmed it. I do.
She had Taeo put his palm flat on a reading plate. When he leaned on it, she reminded him it wasn't a scale.
His output was low. She wouldn't assign a rank yet. Taeo had hoped magic would make him harder to replace.
Then Chae asked Nib to raise his left hand. Nib asked why. Because I asked, she said.
That told her something. A construct doesn't ask why. Nib wasn't responding like an ordinary summon.
The problem was the form. It only had two boxes. A construct was registered equipment, like a courier's golem. A person needed an ID and an awakening record. Nib had no ID.
Nib said, I'm not a box. So Chae decided to write down exactly what he said.
The moment she did, her screen turned red. Anomalous entity. Notify the Kanghan Institute, under state contract.
Chae had never seen that alert before. Taeo asked what Kanghan was.
But Nib was looking at the glass door. Someone was already standing outside it. He brought two cups, Nib said.
